formulas.name: Breadth-first search (Moore 1959)

formulas.name: Pruefer encoding (Pruefer 1918)
formulas.where: A bijection between labelled trees on \(n\) nodes and sequences in \(V^{n-2}\), so there are \(n^{n-2}\) trees (Cayley). It needs an ordered node set. Each node appears in \(P\) exactly \(\deg(v)-1\) times.

formulas.name: Decoding
formulas.latex: e_i=\{\min\{v\notin\{p_i,\dots,p_{n-2}\}\cup\{\ell_1,\dots,\ell_{i-1}\}\},\ p_i\},\qquad \text{the last edge joins the two nodes left}
formulas.where: Rebuild the tree by pairing each \(p_i\) with the smallest node that no longer appears later in the sequence.

variants.nxs_prufer: The encoding of a tree as its sequence.
variants.nxs_from_prufer: The tree rebuilt from a sequence, edges added in the order of decoding.
